This is because each packet must carry additional information that must be transmitted and received. On the other hand, data redundancy can also improve packet arrival times by helping to ensure the accuracy and integrity of the data being transmitted. By including error-correcting codes and other forms of redundancy, data can be checked and cor- rected for errors before it is transmitted, reducing the need for retransmissions and improving overall network efﬁ- ciency. In general, the relationship between packet arrival time and data redundancy will depend on a variety of factors, including the speciﬁc application, the network environment, and the amount of redundancy being used. By carefully balancing the need for data redundancy with the need for efﬁcient and timely packet transmission, net- work engineers can optimize network performance and ensure reliable data transmission [ 30]

Sadly, component errors (Fig. 1c) are a critical factor limiting the size of such circuits.
